title: Precision Without Waste — The Oli Difference
bodyHtml:
Oli 74 (Mechanical) in-wall cistern — controlled sequencing for consistent long-term performance, paired with Futura wall hung pan by Hatria.

Precision Without Waste — The Oli Difference

A different approach to water efficiency in concealed cistern systems — based on sequencing, not reduction.

Water efficiency is typically measured in litres per flush. Oli approaches it differently — through sequencing.

Rather than reducing how much water is used, the system focuses on how precisely the flush cycle is controlled. A small shift in how a system operates can deliver meaningful efficiency without compromising performance.

Oli 74 (Pneumatic) In Wall Cistern — consistent performance across wall faced and wall hung applications.

A simple shift in how a system works

In conventional cistern systems, refill can begin while discharge is still occurring. Water re-enters the tank before the discharge valve has fully sealed, creating overlap within the same flush cycle. Oli’s delayed refill technology removes this overlap entirely.

The inlet valve remains closed until discharge has fully completed. Refill begins only once the discharge valve has sealed. The cycle becomes sequential rather than concurrent.

This separation is subtle, but it changes how efficiently the system resets.

Fig. 1 — Refill Timing Comparison

Standard vs delayed refill sequencing

Standard systems allow overlap. Oli separates the cycle.

How delayed refill works — separating discharge and refill to eliminate unnecessary water inflow during each cycle.

Efficiency without compromise

This approach saves approximately 0.5 litres per flush.

Importantly, the saving is not achieved by reducing flush performance. The system continues to deliver the full rated 4.5/3L flush volume.

Efficiency is achieved through control, not restriction.

Because this performance is embedded within the refill architecture, it does not rely on user behaviour or reduced capacity. It is consistent across every use, over the life of the system.

From individual fixture to building scale

At the level of a single fixture, the saving is incremental. Across a building, it compounds.

Whether in residential homes, multi-residential developments, or hospitality environments, small per-cycle reductions accumulate into a measurable decrease in total water use over time. Over a typical 20-year asset life, the cumulative impact becomes significant — particularly in high-frequency environments.

In commercial settings, water use also directly influences wastewater discharge. Reducing flush volume reduces both incoming water demand and outgoing discharge within a usage-based system.

The impact is not immediate or visible. But over time, it is measurable.

Fig. 2 — Annual Water Savings at Scale

Cumulative impact of 0.5L saved per flush

Small per-cycle savings compound into measurable impact at scale.

Designed for specification

Oli’s delayed refill technology is integrated across its concealed cistern systems, allowing consistent performance regardless of application.

Oli 74 is a compact in-wall system suited to space-efficient installations, with front-access servicing and flexible actuation options.

Expert Evo is a low-level and under-bench system designed for more complex structural applications, with flexible servicing access and integrated frame options.

Across both systems, refill sequencing remains consistent, meeting required WELS ratings and relevant standards.

Compliance defines the baseline — sequencing precision extends it.

Encore by Mingara — Oli 74 in-wall cisterns specified for reliable performance and controlled water use across a high-demand hospitality environment.

Engineered performance, over time

Water efficiency can be specified. System performance must be engineered.

Oli concealed cistern systems apply controlled refill sequencing to reduce water use without reducing performance — delivering a more precise and efficient outcome over the life of a building.

Precision without waste is not a claim. It is engineered performance.
